metadata.title: KD-FixMatch: Knowledge Distillation Siamese Neural Networks

nodes.name: Siamese Neural Network (SNN)
nodes.statement: A Siamese Neural Network (SNN) consists of two identical weight-sharing classifier networks, a teacher and a student. The teacher receives a weakly augmented image and generates pseudo labels, while the student receives a strongly augmented image.

nodes.name: FixMatch Optimization Problem
nodes.statement: The FixMatch optimization problem is min_{theta} f(theta), where f(theta) = (1/2C) theta^T theta + (1/ell) sum_{i=1}^{ell} xi(theta; x^i, y^i), with C > 0 a regularization parameter, x^i the i-th input image, and y^i the one-hot label vector.

nodes.name: FixMatch Loss Function
nodes.statement: The loss function xi(theta; x^i, y^i) is defined piecewise: xi_l(y^i, f_theta(x^i_w)) if i is in the labeled set S_l, and lambda_u * xi_u(y_hat^i, f_theta(x^i_s)) if i is in the unlabeled set S_u, where x^i_w and x^i_s are weak and strong augmentations, respectively.

nodes.name: FixMatch Confidence Filtering
nodes.statement: The unlabeled loss uses a confidence threshold tau: 1(max(y_hat^i) >= tau) * xi_u(OHL(y_hat^i), f_theta(x^i_s)), where 1 is the indicator function and OHL maps the softmax pseudo label to its one-hot label vector. Only pseudo labels with confidence above tau are used.

nodes.name: Symmetric Loss Function
nodes.statement: A loss function xi is called symmetric if it satisfies sum_{k=1}^{K} xi(f(x), e_k) = M for all x in X and all f, where K is the number of classes, X is the feature space, f maps input x to softmax output y, M is a constant, and e_k are standard basis vectors.

nodes.name: Trusted Pseudo Label Selection
nodes.statement: After the outer SNN is trained, pseudo labels are generated for unlabeled data. A threshold tau^{select} filters high-confidence predictions, then deep embedding clustering on latent representations selects unlabeled data whose clustering results are consistent with their predicted class. The chosen indices form the trusted set T_u.

nodes.name: Merging Conflict Pseudo Labels (Heuristic 1)
nodes.statement: When both the outer and inner SNN provide trusted pseudo labels for the same image, conflicts are resolved by a priority heuristic: (1) if the inner SNN's pseudo label confidence exceeds tau^{inner}, use the inner SNN's label; (2) else if the index is in T_u, use the outer SNN's label; (3) otherwise, set the pseudo label to zero (no contribution).

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement: Given labeled data S_l and unlabeled data S_u: (1) Initialize and train an outer SNN f^{outer} with S_l and S_u by solving the FixMatch optimization problem; (2) Generate pseudo labels for S_u using the well-trained f^{outer}; (3) Select a trusted index subset T_u from S_u via confidence filtering and deep embedding clustering; (4) Choose CE or robust loss for xi^{inner}_u; (5) Initialize and train an inner SNN f^{inner} with labeled data, unlabeled data, and unlabeled data with trusted pseudo labels; (6) Return the well-trained f^{inner}.

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch Has Better Starting Point
nodes.statement: KD-FixMatch has a better training starting point than directly applying FixMatch because the outer SNN is first well-trained and its network serves as a teacher for the inner SNN, producing pseudo labels with lower label noise especially in the early training stage.
assumptions: The outer SNN is well-trained before generating pseudo labels for the inner SNN
The percentage of label noise in pseudo labels generated by the well-trained outer SNN is lower than that of the immature teacher in standard FixMatch, especially in the early stage
conclusions: KD-FixMatch has a better training starting point than FixMatch
The better starting point leads to improved model performance

nodes.name: Single Training Pass Sufficiency
nodes.statement: Unlike self-training or Noisy Student where the neural network is re-trained multiple times when pseudo labels need updating, KD-FixMatch only requires training each of the outer and inner SNN once.
assumptions: KD-FixMatch uses sequential then simultaneous teacher-student training
The trusted pseudo label selection via confidence filtering and deep embedding clustering is performed once after the outer SNN training
conclusions: Each of the outer and inner SNN needs to be trained only once
This is more efficient than iterative self-training approaches that re-train and re-generate pseudo labels multiple times

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch Outperforms FixMatch
nodes.statement: Experimental results on SVHN, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and FOOD101 demonstrate that KD-FixMatch outperforms FixMatch in all tested cases, though the improvement diminishes with more labeled data.
assumptions: Experiments are conducted on four public datasets (SVHN, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, FOOD101)
EfficientNet-B0 pretrained on ImageNet is used as the backbone
All methods use the same optimizer (Adam), batch size (128), and augmentation strategies
conclusions: FixMatch outperforms supervised Baseline in all cases
KD-FixMatch outperforms FixMatch in all cases
The improvement of KD-FixMatch over FixMatch decreases as the amount of labeled data increases
KD-FixMatch-SCE has slightly better performance than KD-FixMatch-CE in most cases

nodes.name: Robust Loss Functions Improve Performance
nodes.section: 4.1 Experiments on Four Public Data Sets
nodes.statement: KD-FixMatch-SCE (using symmetric cross-entropy as the unlabeled loss for the inner SNN) achieves slightly better model performance than KD-FixMatch-CE in most cases, even without grid search for the SCE parameters (alpha, beta).
assumptions: SCE is used with alpha=1.0 and beta in {0.01, 0.1} without exhaustive parameter search
SCE is applied only to the inner SNN's unlabeled loss xi^{inner}_u
conclusions: SCE-based KD-FixMatch slightly outperforms CE-based KD-FixMatch in most experimental settings

nodes.name: Inner SNN Generalizes Better Than Outer SNN
nodes.statement: The inner SNN intuitively has better generalization ability than the outer SNN because it has more reliable pseudo labels available in the early training stage, justifying the priority of the inner SNN's pseudo labels in the merging heuristic.
assumptions: The inner SNN is trained with labeled data, unlabeled data, and additionally with trusted pseudo-labeled data from the outer SNN
The trusted pseudo labels reduce label noise in the early stage of inner SNN training
conclusions: The inner SNN has better generalization ability than the outer SNN
When pseudo label conflicts arise, the inner SNN's pseudo labels should take priority over the outer SNN's
